summary: The governor runs the executive branch, proposes the state budget, signs or vetoes bills, and appoints judges and hundreds of officials. The seat is open: Gavin Newsom is term-limited. In the June 2 top-two primary, Democrat Xavier Becerra (former U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary and former state Attorney General) placed first with 27.98% and Republican Steve Hilton (former adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron and former Fox News host) placed second with 24.59%, edging out Democrat Tom Steyer (22.79%), who spent heavily from his own fortune and later endorsed Becerra. Republicans have not won a California governor's race since 2006.

positions.stance: Supports a progressive income tax and extending the higher rate on high earners to fund schools; opposes Proposition 40, the billionaire wealth tax; has not ruled out raising taxes and would tax corporations whose workers qualify for public health coverage. (CalMatters voter guide)

Would declare a state of emergency to finance about 40,000 approved but unfunded affordable units, push cities to zone for more homes, expand down-payment assistance, and curb large corporations buying homes in bulk. (CalMatters)

Would create ongoing state rental-assistance funding and a public dashboard of state-funded units; says people should not voluntarily stay on the street when offered shelter but stops short of supporting arrests. (CalMatters)

Would declare a state of emergency to freeze utility and insurance rates and crack down on price gouging; supports the state's clean-energy goals but is open to revising them, including the 2035 ban on new gas-car sales, if they make energy unaffordable. (CalMatters)
Supports California's sanctuary law, which he defended in court as Attorney General. (CalMatters)
Former single-payer supporter; now backs expanding coverage to as many residents as possible, cutting insurer administrative spending, and requiring more telehealth coverage. (CalMatters)
Makes confronting the Trump administration central to his campaign, citing the more than 100 lawsuits he filed against the first Trump administration as Attorney General. (CalMatters)

Would eliminate state income tax on the first $150,000 of earnings with a flat rate above that, halve the gas tax, and eliminate the $800 minimum business registration fee; opposes Proposition 40. (CalMatters voter guide)

Aims to 'bring back the starter home' by cutting fees and building rules for small single-family homes, create a state loan program for first-time buyers, and limit CEQA lawsuits; favors suburban development over dense city apartments. (CalMatters)
Treats street camping as illegal and wants police involved in clearing all encampments; would prioritize sober housing over low-barrier shelters. (CalMatters)

Would suspend environmental regulations to lower gas prices (campaign target: $3 a gallon), end mandates requiring utilities to buy solar and wind power, and expand natural gas production. (CalMatters; Wikipedia)
Would overturn the sanctuary law, reopen closed prisons, reduce good-conduct early releases, and loosen firearm restrictions. (CalMatters)
Would end state-funded Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants and redirect the money to lowering costs for legal residents. (CalMatters)
Endorsed by President Trump on April 6, 2026; says a cooperative relationship would help California secure federal funds. (CalMatters; Wikipedia)

key_differences: Income tax: Hilton would exempt the first $150,000 of income from state tax entirely; Becerra keeps the progressive system and wants to extend the higher top rate. At their CNN debate Becerra called Hilton's plan a large tax cut for the wealthiest.

Energy and climate: Hilton would suspend environmental rules and end renewable-purchase mandates to cut gas and power prices; Becerra keeps the clean-energy goals but says he would revisit them, including the 2035 gas-car phase-out, if costs spike.
Immigration: Becerra would keep the sanctuary law he defended in court; Hilton would repeal it and end Medi-Cal for undocumented adults.
Homelessness: Hilton would have police clear every encampment and favors sober housing; Becerra emphasizes rental assistance and declines to back arrests.
Relationship with Washington: Hilton is Trump-endorsed and promises cooperation; Becerra is running as the state's defender against the administration.

polling.result: Becerra 60%, Hilton 33%; with leaners, Becerra 64%, Hilton 36%. Among independents, Becerra 46%, Hilton 36%.
Becerra 58%, Hilton 33%, as reported by MultiState; exact field dates not confirmed in this session.
